design_detail: Official record of a meeting, not a study: the final summary minutes (6 printed pages) of the FDA's Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting of 4 June 2024 on new drug application 215455 (midomafetamine capsules, Lykos Therapeutics, proposed indication PTSD), approved on 26 July 2024 and signed by the committee's designated federal officer and its chair. It records the attendance, the agenda (sponsor and FDA presentations, an open public hearing), a summary of the committee's discussion of four questions and the results of two votes. It summarizes; the verbatim transcript, which it cites for details, was not read. Card design 'narrative-review' is the schema's closest category; the editors' narrative-review checklist is used, its domains read as questions about the minutes as a source. No data or analyses of its own.
can_establish: How the committee voted on effectiveness and on benefit-risk, who voted, and the reasons members gave as the FDA summarized them.
cannot_establish: The FDA's decision or its reasons (the committee is advisory and the minutes precede the decision); how each member voted or reasoned (no vote is attributed); how many members held each view behind words such as some, many or a majority; anything said only in the transcript.

sample.recruitment: Not applicable (meeting record). Voting members: five standing members of the committee present (three absent) and six temporary voting members; one non-voting industry representative; six non-voting FDA participants.
sample.selection_effects: The minutes are a summary written by the FDA; which remarks are summarized, and how, is the FDA's choice.

outcomes.instruments: Two votes (yes, no or abstain) on questions set by the FDA (fda_2024d), after discussion of four further questions.

analysis.effect_sizes: Vote counts only: 2 yes, 9 no, 0 abstentions on effectiveness; 1 yes, 10 no, 0 abstentions on benefit-risk.
analysis.selective_reporting: The discussion is summarized in a paragraph per question, with unquantified attributions (some, many, others); details are deferred to the transcript.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Two clear majority votes against the application and a short summary of the reasons given.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The minutes claim only that they accurately reflect what transpired (the officers' certification, p. 1).

timeline.event: FDA briefing document and erratum distributed to the members before the meeting.
The FDA's questions to the committee.
Meeting of 4 June 2024; minutes approved 26 July 2024 (this document).
The BMJ summarizes these minutes (citing them as dated 30 July 2024) and reports the FDA's rejection of the application (Mahase, 2024).

replication.where_it_stands: The minutes are the primary record of the votes; The BMJ's summary (most members not persuaded of effectiveness; all but one against on benefit-risk) matches them.

funding.funder: US Food and Drug Administration (government regulator).
funding.declared_conflicts: A conflict of interest statement was read into the record (p. 2); its content is not reproduced in the minutes.
funding.affiliations_note: Industry representative (non-voting): Carla M. Canuso. Sponsor presenters included Lykos staff (programme lead, chief scientific officer, senior medical director) and two academic clinicians (Massachusetts General Hospital; NYU Langone).

what_would_settle_it: For what the committee said: the verbatim transcript; for what the FDA decided and why: its decision letter.

domains.note: A summary by the FDA of a day-long meeting; the transcript is the complete record and the minutes defer to it.
Members' reasons are reported without the data or arguments behind them.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: Not applicable in the usual sense; the minutes report the committee, not FDA studies.
Views are attributed to some, many or a majority of members without counts, except for the votes; one sentence on the yes voters' reasoning is ambiguous (reporting issue 1).

domains.domain: Balance of members' views (the minority who voted yes)
domains.note: The reasons of the yes voters are summarized alongside the majority's.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated instrument applies to meeting minutes (METHODS §5.3); the editors' narrative-review checklist is used as the closest available. The minutes are the primary record of the votes and may be cited for them and for the reasons as summarized; for the weight of each reason among members, and for anything said in detail, the transcript is needed.

key_findings.finding: The committee discussed new drug application 215455, midomafetamine (MDMA) capsules submitted by Lykos Therapeutics for PTSD, and was asked to discuss the overall benefit-risk profile including the potential public health impact; the minutes were approved on 26 July 2024 and certified as accurate by the designated federal officer (Joyce Frimpong) and the chair (Rajesh Narendran).
Members had received the FDA's and the sponsor's briefing materials before the meeting; about 1,570 people attended and there were 32 open public hearing presentations.

Voting members present: five standing members (Dunn, Fiedorowicz, Iyengar, Narendran as chair, Witczak as consumer representative; three standing members absent) and six temporary voting members (Amirshahi, Barone and Holtzheimer by video, Hertig, Joniak-Grant as patient representative, Rebo); a non-voting industry representative and six non-voting FDA participants.
key_findings.note: Editors' count: 11 voting members, which matches both vote totals (2 + 9 and 1 + 10).

key_findings.finding: The sponsor presented the unmet need, efficacy, safety, a clinician's perspective and benefit-risk; the FDA presented the background, regulatory history and key issues (clinical reviewer), the efficacy analysis (statistical reviewer), the safety analysis and risk management.

Question 1 (effectiveness): members commented that functional unblinding and expectation bias may have played a role in the results; some said a larger sample would have helped; some said these biases alone could explain the short-term results; on durability, many said the small data set was too confounded to judge; on the psychological intervention, members suggested a two-by-two factorial design, and some were concerned that therapist unblinding and the therapists' power of suggestion could have influenced the results.
key_findings.locator: Questions to the Committee, question 1, Committee Discussion

key_findings.finding: Question 2 (adequacy of the safety data): members suggested data in comorbid populations, and mentioned the risks of boundary violations and hyponatremia, the lack of laboratory data and of QTc and cardiac data; others found the abuse-liability assessment inadequate and raised diversion, while some said these could be addressed in phase 4 studies.
key_findings.locator: Questions to the Committee, question 2, Committee Discussion

key_findings.finding: Question 3 (impairment): members said impairment could last longer than was studied and that a REMS would be needed; others were concerned that tapering other psychotropic medicines could add to impairment; some suggested an overnight stay; members wanted clearer monitoring and discharge criteria (heart rate, blood pressure).
key_findings.locator: Questions to the Committee, question 3, Committee Discussion

key_findings.finding: Question 4 (risk mitigation): many members agreed the risk was not fully characterized and suggested two licensed therapists, training by an independent outside group rather than the sponsor, medical training for therapists, medical staff on site, safety reporting mechanisms outside the treatment centres, more complete ECG, laboratory and vital-sign data, and fuller characterization of the duration of impairment.
key_findings.locator: Questions to the Committee, question 4, Committee Discussion

key_findings.finding: Vote on whether the available data show that the drug is effective in patients with PTSD: yes 2, no 9, abstain 0. Many members said functional unblinding, the lack of management of expectation bias, and selection bias limited the interpretability of the efficacy analyses; the yes voters shared the concerns about unblinding and expectation bias but gave decisive weight to the large effect sizes.
key_findings.locator: Question 5, Vote Result and Committee Discussion

key_findings.finding: Vote on whether the benefits of midomafetamine with the FDA's proposed REMS outweigh its risks for patients with PTSD: yes 1, no 10, abstain 0. Many members said more efficacy and safety data were needed; the one yes voter judged the REMS, while not perfect, on the right track and stressed the need for new PTSD treatments.
key_findings.locator: Question 6, Vote Result and Committee Discussion

reporting_issues.issue: The yes voters are said to have had concerns about unblinding and expectation bias that "could have reduced the effect size that were reported"; the sentence most plausibly means that the true effect may be smaller than reported, but its wording is ambiguous.
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite it as the yes voters accepting the bias concerns and weighing the large effect sizes; do not cite a direction of bias from it.

reporting_issues.issue: Selection bias is named among the reasons for the no votes without saying what selection is meant.
reporting_issues.consequence: The FDA briefing document (fda_2024a, pp. 37-38) discusses selection into the follow-up study; whether members meant that or recruitment into the trials cannot be told from the minutes.

verification.source_read: PDF pp. 1-6 (PDFs/MDMA/FDA_2024_AdvisoryMinutes.pdf), read in full from the text layer; the vote tables on p. 6 are plain text.
